title: Germany – Ships and boats – Marine-Hafenschlepper und flexibler Fähigkeitsträger (Navy-Tug flex) - TNW
description: Für die Deutsche Marine sind über eine Rahmenvereinbarung bis zu 20 baugleiche Hafenschlepper mit Arbeitsdeck der Klasse 724, die den Vorgaben einer anerkannten Klassifikationsgesellschaft und der deutschen Flagge entsprechen, aus einer bereits laufenden Serienproduktion neu zu beschaffen. Dabei ist über den Einsatz als reinen Schlepper hinaus eine zusätzliche Verwendung als "flexibler Fähigkeitsträger" beabsichtigt, welcher die Aufnahme von zwei ISO 20-Fuß-Standardcontainern bzw. vier ISO 10-Fuß-Containern und eine technische Seeausdauer von mindestens sieben Tagen ermöglicht. Aufgrund der aktuellen sicherheitspolitischen Lage ist zum Zwecke der Eindämmung des laufenden hybriden Krieges Russlands gegen die Bundesrepublik Deutschland und ihre Verbündeten im Nord- und Ostseeraum eine kurzfristige Beschaffung (bis 2028) erforderlich. Ziel ist es, die bei der Deutschen Marine derzeit vorhandenen sechs ca. 35 Jahre alten, nicht mehr bedarfsdeckenden Hafenschlepper der Klasse 725 zu ersetzen. Die vorgenannten Hafenschlepper werden insbesondere für die Erfüllung nachfolgender Einsatzaufgaben beschafft: • Assistenz/Bugsieren/Manövrieren von Schiffen und Booten der Marine auf Reeden und im Hafen, • Schleppen von Marineschiffen, -booten und Geräten im Hafen und im küstennahen Seegebiet, • Begleiten von Seezielschießen inkl. Transport, Ausbringen und Schleppen von Seezielen, • Aufnahme von zwei ISO 20-Fuß- Standardcontainern bzw. vier ISO 10-Fuß-Containern, • Unterstützung bei Werfterprobungen, Standproben und Kompensationsfahrten, • Eisdienst in den Häfen, • Brandbekämpfung im Hafen und auf See, • Hilfeleistung bei Gewässerverunreinigung sowie • Sicherung und Bergung von Schiffen und Booten in See.

title: North Atlantic Right Whale Density Model Outputs and Scientific Support for Entanglement Risk Assessment
description: The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) has a requirement to provide scientific advice on the risks of North Atlantic right whale entanglements in non-tended fixed fishing gear to inform management decisions. The Contractor must provide customized North Atlantic Right Whale (NARW) Density Surface Model (DSM) outputs, along with scientific consultation to support DFO’s entanglement risk assessment. This includes advice on model structure, assumptions, limitations, uncertainty, interpretation, and application; participation in assessment and technical discussions; and post-assessment support. The work will involve the following: 1. Tasks 1.1 Generate Customized Density Model Outputs The Contractor must generate customized density model outputs according to the Project Authority’s requirements. 1.2 Provide Scientific Consultation The Contractor must provide scientific consultation on model assumptions, limitations, uncertainty, interpretation, and application. 1.3 Participate in Technical Meetings and Assessment Activities The Contractor must participate in a kick-off meeting, approximately one technical meeting per month, additional discussions as required, and CSAS assessment and peer review activities, as requested by the Project Authority. The CSAS assessment is currently planned for December 2027 or January 2028. 1.4 Provide Post-Assessment Support The Contractor must provide post-assessment scientific clarification and technical support, as required by the Project Authority. 2. Deliverables and Acceptance Criteria 2.1 Customized Density Model Outputs The Contractor must provide customized density model outputs for the Gulf of St. Lawrence and Cabot Strait to support the entanglement risk assessment and scenario evaluation. The outputs must include: • Weekly density estimates. • Associated standard errors for the weekly density estimates. • Summary tables and spatial products, as required. • Supporting documentation. Outputs will be provided at the original 5 km grid resolution or aggregated or transformed to DFO’s defined 10 km² hexagonal grid, as required by the Project Authority. Acceptance Criteria The deliverable will be accepted when the Project Authority confirms that the outputs: • Are provided in the agreed electronic format. • Cover the requested spatial and temporal areas. • Include weekly density estimates and associated standard errors. • Include sufficient supporting information to understand and use the outputs for the intended assessment. Delivery Date Initial outputs must be delivered no later than March 31, 2027. Revisions or supplementary outputs will be provided according to timelines established by the Project Authority in consultation with the Contractor. 2.2 Final Technical Report The Contractor must provide a final technical report documenting the density model outputs and relevant technical information to support DFO’s entanglement risk assessment. Acceptance Criteria The final technical report will be accepted when the Project Authority confirms that it has been provided in the agreed electronic format and contains the technical information required to support the assessment. Delivery Date The Contractor must submit the final technical report on or before April 30, 2028.

title: Germany – Network equipment – Rahmenvertrag Netzwerkkomponenten 2027, Verlängerung Cisco EA
description: Die Bayerischen Staatsforsten AöR betreiben eine hochverfügbare, zentral administrierte IT- und Kommunikationsinfrastruktur zur Unterstützung der Geschäfts- und Produktionsprozesse an rund 600 Standorten, Außenstellen, Rechenzentrumsstandorten und Homeoffice-Arbeitsplätzen. Die Infrastruktur umfasst lokale Netzwerke (LAN), standortübergreifende Weitverkehrsverbindungen (WAN), Netzwerksicherheitslösungen, WLAN-Infrastrukturen, Sprachkommunikationssysteme sowie zentrale Management- und Automatisierungsplattformen. Zur Sicherstellung eines sicheren, stabilen und wirtschaftlichen Betriebs werden die Netzwerkdienste zentral gesteuert, überwacht und administriert. Die Netzwerkinfrastruktur verbindet die Standorte der Auftraggeberin mit den Rechenzentren und stellt die Grundlage für den Zugriff auf Fachanwendungen, Kommunikationsdienste und digitale Geschäftsprozesse dar. Die Infrastruktur wird kontinuierlich erweitert, modernisiert und an neue technische, organisatorische und sicherheitsrelevante Anforderungen angepasst. Für die Netzwerke der Bayerischen Staatsforsten kommen ausschließlich Netzwerkkomponenten (Hardware, Software, Software-Dienste) der Fa. Cisco zum Einsatz. Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrages über die Lieferung von Netzwerkkomponenten des Herstellers Cisco einschließlich zugehöriger Software, Lizenzen, Wartungs-, Pflege-, Support- und Instandhaltungsleistungen sowie gegebenenfalls weiterer technischer Dienstleistungen. Auf Basis des Rahmenvertrages sollen bestehende Komponenten während der Vertragslaufzeit bedarfsgerecht erneuert, erweitert oder ersetzt werden. Der Rahmenvertrag dient nicht dem vollständigen Neuaufbau einer isolierten Infrastruktur, sondern der Weiterentwicklung einer bestehenden, produktiv betriebenen Netzwerklandschaft im laufenden Betrieb auf Basis von Netzwerkkomponenten. Die zu beschaffenden Leistungen müssen sich in die bestehende Systemlandschaft integrieren lassen und die Anforderungen an Interoperabilität, Informationssicherheit, Verfügbarkeit, Betriebsstabilität, Administrierbarkeit und Wirtschaftlichkeit erfüllen. Besondere Bedeutung kommt dabei der Kompatibilität mit vorhandenen Netzwerk-, Sicherheits-, Management- und Automatisierungsprozessen sowie der Fähigkeit zu, den Betrieb der bestehenden Infrastruktur ohne unverhältnismäßige Umstellungs-, Migrations- oder Parallelbetriebsaufwände sicherzustellen. Der geschätzte Gesamtbedarf umfasst die sukzessive Beschaffung von Netzwerkkomponenten, Netzwerksicherheitslösungen, Softwarelizenzen sowie zugehörigen Wartungs-, Pflege-, Support- und Instandhaltungsleistungen über die vorgesehene Vertragslaufzeit. Die Leistungen werden bedarfsabhängig durch Einzelabrufe aus dem Rahmenvertrag bezogen

title: Ballfield Maintenance
description: The United States Coast Guard Academy intends to solicit quotations for ballfield maintenance services at the Nitchman Field Complex in New London, Connecticut. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to maintain the Baseball, Softball, and track-and-field/practice soccer fields in accordance with NCAA specifications. Required services include seasonal late-winter/early-spring maintenance of the baseball and softball infields and turf areas, including scarifying, regrading, infield and warning-track material placement, lip removal, edging, rolling, turf repair, replacement and verification of home plates and pitching rubbers, baseline and mound adjustments, and bullpen and pitching-mound repairs. The contractor shall also perform June deep-tine hollow-core aeration and topdressing of all three fields. The anticipated contract consists of a one-year base period, January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2027, with four one-year option periods.

title: REKONSTRUKCE BALKONŮ
description: 1) Předmětem plnění zadávané Veřejné zakázky je odstranění havarijního stavu balkonových konstrukcí a zábradlí, a to 4 (čtyř) balkonů ve 2. NP Objektu II v areálu zadavatele na adrese Na Hranicích 674/18, 181 00 Praha 8 – Bohnice, dle požadavků uvedených v této Výzvě, v závazném návrhu smlouvy o dílo a v jejích přílohách – Příloze č. 1 Smlouvy – Položkový rozpočet (soupis prací s výkazem výměr) a Příloze č. 2 Smlouvy – Technická specifikace. 2) Předmětem plnění jsou zejména tyto činnosti: a) odstranění poškozených výplní zábradlí (pletivo, drátosklo) a poškozených prodlužovacích roštů pochozích ploch balkonů; b) odstranění původní pochozí plochy až na nosnou konstrukci balkonů; c) sanace nosné konstrukce balkonů (nad i pod) včetně nátěru kovových částí; d) provedení nové hydroizolace a povrchové úpravy pochozí plochy protiskluzovou dlažbou, včetně sanace kovového lože pro nové prodlužovací rošty a okapnice navazující na hydroizolaci; e) dodávka a montáž nových výplní zábradlí (pletivo a drátosklo v novém kovovém rámu) a prodlužovacích roštů v žárově zinkovaném provedení; f) broušení a nátěr konstrukce zábradlí a obnova nátěru fasády; g) zřízení, pronájem a odstranění lešení, zajištění přístupu na balkony výhradně z vnější strany objektu a ochrana přilehlých pokojů klientů (izolace oken a dveří proti hluku a prachu); h) demontáž a zpětná montáž sítě proti ptákům, fyzická ostraha staveniště včetně lešení v době nepřítomnosti pracovníků, průběžný a závěrečný úklid a likvidace odpadů v souladu s právními předpisy; i) předání atestů, certifikátů a prohlášení o shodě použitých materiálů a výrobků a další smlouvou vymezené požadavky na předmět plnění. j) Stavební práce budou prováděny za plného provozu pobytového zařízení sociálních služeb. Práce lze provádět pouze ve všední dny, a to v době 9:00–11:00 hod. a 14:00–16:30 hod., nedohodnou-li se smluvní strany jinak (blíže viz závazný návrh smlouvy o dílo).

Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The challenge is to provide the Department of National Defense (DND) and the Canadian Army (CA) a software solution to provide an airspace common operating picture so that it can plan, deconflict, and control uncrewed aircraft system (UAS) traffic, including their use of the radio frequency (RF) spectrum, in order to ensure the safe and efficient management of UAS to enable the Canadian soldier to successfully fight and survive on the future battlefield. Details: Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Be Windows-based. 2. Allow a user to create and store flight plans, including radio frequency requirements. 3. Have a flight plan repository (database) that stores the 4D (3D + time) trajectories and spectrum requirements of all accepted flight plans. 4. Enable integration of supplemental data services such as crewed aircraft flight plans and weather. 5. Generate an optimal 4D flight path for UAS based on specific mission goals and physical limits. 6. Be able to check new flight requests against existing flight plans, airspace constraints (no-fly zones) and RF spectrum requests to detect conflicts and resolve them (via set priorities or a human decision). 7. Generate 4D blocks of deconflicted airspace (a "tunnel" or a "box") where a UAS is permitted to fly. Additional Outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Analyze real-time data from UASs to prevent collisions and automatically adjust flight paths for UASs in controlled airspace. 2. Check in real-time whether a UAS is following its pre-approved, deconflicted trajectory. 3. Demonstrate capacity in having its critical components produced and sourced in countries within the NATO alliance, NATO Partners or Major Non-NATO Allies. To achieve this, Offerors are requested to provide as an attachment to their proposal, a list identifying the solution's critical components, the country of production and sourcing for each component. Critical components and requested information for each Critical components are defined below: Critical components: 1. Radio 2. Ground control station (GCS) 3. On-board computer 4. Any software Requested information: i. Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM): Name of the original equipment manufacturer of the product being sourced ii. OEM URL: Provide the URL of the OEM iii. Software: Confirm if developed by Offeror or outsourced iv. Product name: Provide the OEM's product name v. Model number: Provide the OEM's model and/or version number of the product vi. Product URL: Provide the URL of the OEM product, model, and version vii. Country of origin IMPORTANT NOTE: For this challenge, kindly disregard the Attachment requirements detailed at Section D in the Web-Portal, and instead adhere to the following: - The attachment measures 8.5" by 11" with a maximum size of 10Mb. - Only the following formats will be accepted: JPG, GIF, TIF, PDF or PNG. - The attachment must be clear and legible. Note: Including an attachment is not mandatory, but forms part of the Additional Outcomes, which is scored up to 10 points. The Applicant (Offeror) acknowledges that it is within Canada's sole discretion to determine whether the attachment is removed or included in the Offer. The transformative changes being made are conceptually described in the CA publication Inflection Point 2025. This document provides the broad context for modernization and directs the development and acquisition of key systems; in particular, it states: Key to this transformation is the integration of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, robotics, autonomous and uncrewed systems. These capabilities will support a wide range of functions, from intelligence analysis and predictive modeling to targeting and operational execution. The CA, in recognizing this need, has purchased foreign robotics and autonomous systems of varying quality and has identified challenges purchasing systems that meet operational requirements, in particular related to cold-weather operations, and that have stable supply chains. Further, purchases have, in the past, been constrained by limited manufacturing capacity of industry partners. To address this, the Government of Canada's recently released policy Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, emphasizes the need to develop a strong domestic industrial capacity to produce defence materiel. This policy directs the CA to seek solutions to operational problems through Canadian industry, which will both improve the CA's capability while providing the foundation of a strong defence industrial base able to scale production of quality defence material. title: Perusterveydenhuollon hoidon jatkuvuuden ammatinharjoittajamallin hankinta
description: Perusterveydenhuollon hoidon jatkuvuuden ammatinharjoittajamallin hankinta Hankinnan kohteena on yleislääkäripalveluiden hankinta ammatinharjoittajamallilla toteutettuna Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankinta sisältää yhteensä neljän (4) lääkärin ostopalvelun Hatanpään sosiaali- ja terveysaseman ja Tammelakeskuksen sosiaali- ja terveysaseman alueiden omapotilaiden hoidon toteuttamiseksi. Ammatinharjoittajamallilla tuotetaan yleislääkäripalvelut kokonaisvaltaisesti hoidon jatkuvuusmallin kriteerien mukaisille omapotilaille, jotka asuvat yrittäjälääkärille osoitetun sote-aseman alueella. Yrittäjälääkäri toimii omalääkärinä, joka on hoitovastuussa omapotilaistaan. Omalääkärin työparina toimii omahoitaja. Yrittäjälääkäri toimii yhteistyössä tilaajan henkilöstön kanssa osana sote-aseman moniammatillista toimintaympäristöä. Palvelussa keskeistä ovat hoidon saatavuuden sekä hoidon jatkuvuuden parantaminen. Palvelu tuotetaan joko edellä mainituilla Tilaajan sosiaali- ja terveysasemilla tai Palveluntuottajan järjestämissä toimitiloissa. Toimitiloja koskevat sijaintivaatimukset on määritetty hankintasopimuksen liitteessä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Sopimuskausi alkaa 1.2.2027 ja on voimassa toistaiseksi. Hankinnan ennakoitu arvonlisäveroton vuosiarvo sitoumuksetta on noin 875 000 euroa. Palveluntuottajien valinta on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön kohdassa ”Päätöksenteon perusteet”. Hankinnan kohde ja vähimmäisvaatimukset on kuvattu tarjouspyynnössä ja tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.,

title: Finland – Domestic appliances – Espoon Asunnot Oy / Kodinkoneiden toimitus, -asennus ja -huolto puitesopimus 2027
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Kodinkoneiden toimitus, -asennus ja -huolto palvelujen tuottaminen Espoon Asunnot Oy:n omistamissa kiinteistöissä. Palvelu sisältää mm.: • Kodinkoneiden tarkastus-, korjaus ja huoltopalvelut • Kodinkoneiden toimituspalvelut • Kodinkoneiden asennuspalvelut • seuranta, raportointi ja dokumentointi • neuvonta tilaajille ja asukkaille Palvelu tuotetaan tilausten perusteella tilaajan kiinteistöissä. Valinta Hankinta jaetaan pääsääntöisesti maantieteellisiin osiin. Hankintayksikkö tekee toimittajan puitesopimus, johon valitaan kaksi palveluntuottajaa. Sopimus tulisi olemaan kestoltaan 4 vuotta. Hankinta on jaettu kahteen maantieteelliseen alueeseen sekä uudiskohteiden laitteisiin ilman asennusta. Kahdelle alueelle valitaan kumppani hoitamaan kodinkoneiden toimitukset ja huolto. Kilpailutuksessa seuraavaksi halvimman molempia alueita tarjonnut valitaan varasijalle, jonka kanssa voidaan tehdä sopimus, jos jomman kumman valitun kanssa ei sopimukseen päästä tai sopimus päätetään kesken sopimuksen. Halvempi tarjoaja saa valita eteläinen vai pohjoinen alue. Uudis- ja peruskorjauskohteet eivät välttämättä noudata samaa aluejakoa. Vaihtoehdot sopimuksen toteuttamisessa ovat seuraavat: 1. Tarjouksen antava yritys voi itse hoitaa sekä kodinkoneiden toimituksen että huollon. 2. Tarjouksen antava yritys toimii kodinkoneiden toimittajana ja yrityksen alihankkija tekee kodinkoneiden huollot. Koko palvelu on kuitenkin tarjottava yhtenä sopimuksena ja kaikki palvelut laskutettava saman toimittajan toimesta Hankinnan kohteena on Espoon Asunnot Oy:n kodinkoneiden toimitukset, -huolto ja -asennuspalvelut. Tilaajalla on tarve molemmilla alueilla noin 1500 kodinkoneen uusimiselle ja 1000 uudelle kodinkoneelle sekä noin 3000 huolto-/asennuskäyntiä per vuosi. Tilaaja ei voi kertoa tarkkoja määriä ennalta eikä luvata tiettyä määrää töitä tai laitteita sopimusaikana. Hintalistan määräarviot ovat ainoastaan tarjousten vertailua varten. Hankinta jaetaan kahteen osaan: Osa 1: Etelä Osa 2: Pohjoinen Hinnoitellaan erikseen: Uudis- ja peruskorjauskohteen kodinkoneet Uudis ja peruskorjauskohteissa lähtökohtaisesti noudatetaan samaa aluejakoa. Kaikkia alueita tarjotaan samalla tarjouksella. Tilaaja valitsee yhteensä 2 sopimuskumppania. Tarjoaja voi käyttää sopimuksen toteuttamisessa myös alihankkijaa eli tarjoaja voi - hoitaa kodinkoneiden toimituksen, -asennus ja huoltopalvelut itse - hoitaa kodinkoneiden toimituksen ja yrityksen alihankkija hoitaa kuljetus-, asennus- ja huoltopalvelut. Tilaaja kuitenkin asioi vain sopimuskumppanin kautta ja vain sopimuskumppani laskuttaa tilaajaa yhdellä laskulla per tilaus. Toimittaja valitaan halvimpien vertailuhintojen perusteella Tarjouksen hintalomakkeessa tulee ilmoittaa arvonlisäverolliset hinnat työselostuksessa kuvattujen työsisältöjen perusteella. description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos pyytää tarjoustanne sopimuksen solmimiseksi pesulapalveluista Maanpuolustuskorkeakoululle Santahaminataloon sopimuskaudelle 01.02.2027-31.12.2030. Majoitustilojen tekstiilien pesulapalvelut seuraavasti: - Vuodevaatteet (lakana, pussilakana, ja tyynyliina, puuvilla) - Pyyhkeet (kylpypyyhe ja käsipyyhe, froteinen) - Patjansuojus (muovikankainen) - Lisäksi muuta kilopyykkiä (harjoitusvarusteita, kuten kypärän suojukset, liiviit ja päähineet) Puolustusvoimien kansainvälinen keskus kuuluu Maanpuolustuskorkeakouluun ja suorittaa kurssitoimintaansa Santahamina-talossa Santahaminassa. Santahamina-talossa on 66 kahden hengen majoitushuonetta, joissa majoittuvat PVKVK:n järjestämien kurssien ja tilaisuuksien kansainväliset osallistujat. Lisäksi majoitustiloja käytetään MPKK:n tarpeisiin.

title: Finland – Construction work – Virtain pelastus- ja ensihoitoaseman hankinta
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Virtain pelastus- ja ensihoitoasema vuokrahankintana Virtain kaupungin osoittamalle tontille. Vuokranantaja rakennuttaa vuokrakohteen siten, että vuokranantaja vastaa vuokrakohteen suunnittelusta, rakennuttamisesta ja ylläpidosta kustannuksellaan. Vuokranantaja saa korvauksen kustannuksista vuokrasopimuksissa sovitun vuokran muodossa. Hankkeeseen valittu tarjoaja on rakennushankkeeseen ryhtyvä, investori, rakennuttaja, päätoteuttaja ja vuokranantaja sekä kiinteistön haltija ja rakennuksen omistaja. Pirkanmaan hyvinvointialue tulee toimimaan vuokralaisena ja käyttäjänä vähintään 20 vuoden ajan.

title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 18 November 2026 at 9:00AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses, and to also provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2028 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $37 million Magnitude of Construction: $100 - $500 million Project Title: Tampa Harbor Improvements Industry Day. Purpose: The purpose of this scheduled Industry Day is to provide the latest information regarding the future advertisement and award of Contract 1 for the Tampa Harbor Deepening Project. The scheduled event will include a detailed presentation by the Jacksonville District US Army Corps of Engineers, Tampa Harbor Project Delivery Team (PDT) followed by open Q&A and 1-1 meeting opportunities with contracts to ask more in-depth questions and get feedback as the design and permitting moves forward. Project Description: The project includes construction dredging to deepen and widen specified areas within the federal navigation channel of Tampa Harbor. The project is planned for six (6) contracts over an estimated 8�10-year period. The Scope of Work for this Industry Day will be focused on Contract 1. Contract 1 work includes deepening of Cut-C (HB), Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, East Bay Channel and Cut-D (HB) to a depth of 49 feet MLLW, deepening the Port Sutton Terminal Channel to a depth of 44 feet MLLW, and deepening the East Bay Channel Extensions 1 and 2 to a depth of 41 feet MLLW. The Contract 1 work also includes widening of Port Sutton Channel, Port Sutton Turning Basin, and East Bay Channel. All areas of deepening and widening will incorporate +1 foot of allowable overdepth. All dredged material from the project will be disposed of in the East Bay Placement Area, DMMA 2-D and DMMA 3-D. Estimated quantities to be dredged are roughly 4.4 million cubic yards. Link to the Tampa Harbor Improvements USACE website: https://www.saj.usace.army.mil/Tampa-Harbor/-30-/ Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: 1. Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. 2. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? 3. Describe the proposed construction methods and sequencing and equipment needed to complete the project. At a minimum, address pre-dredging, side-casting of pre-dredging material, and placement into the East Bay Placement Area including constructing the containment perimeter and filling within the area. The contract will include geologic data of the dredge and placement areas as well as the geotechnical requirements for materials considered suitable for constructing the containment perimeter. The contractor will propose the dredging sequence to accomplish constructing the containment perimeter that meets required geotechnical specifications. Describe the factors considered in determining the dredging sequence, such as the material type, proposed equipment, proximity to the placement area, etc.? 4. Describe any constructability, stability, safety concerns with East Bay Placement Area. Describe additional equipment or methods required to place infill above water and/or above the proposed crest of the containment perimeter. Describe any concerns for drainage of the placement area. 5. Describe how filling the East Bay Placement Area will not result in material migrating out of the placement area and into the federal channel. At a minimum, address how existing soft material at the placement area will be contained when disturbed. 6. Will the proposed East Bay Placement Area construction methods require equipment to be located within the federal channel for extended periods of time acting as obstructions for vessel traffic, or obstruct Port Tampa Bay Berth 150? 7. For East Bay Placement Area, describe any temporal facilities, staging and laydown areas, and utilities that would be required or preferred in adjacent upland areas. 8. Dredging and placement of material will be conducted in a manner to minimize turbidity. Describe the turbidity control measures, such as turbidity curtains, that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If hydraulic placement of infill is proposed for the East Bay Placement Area, describe how affluent will be managed. 9. Based on prior dredging construction experience either in Tampa Bay or other locations in Florida, what are some of the challenges USACE could streamline to improve contract execution? 10. Describe any concerns with execution of the environmental species monitoring and reporting. Event Date: Wednesday, 18 November 2026 at 9:00 AM EST. Event Location: Port of Tampa � Cruise Terminal 6 1331 McKay Street Tampa, Florida 33602 *Parking available onsite For more information, please see the Industry Day Agenda copy under the Attachments. Contact Info: Manny Vianzon, Project Manager (904) 232-3292 Emmanuel.A.Vianzon@usace.army.mil If you cannot attend in person: Link Meeting: https://www.microsoft.com/EN-US/MICROSOFT-TEAMS/JOIN-A-MEETING Meeting ID: 993 212 869 457 Passcode: tG6Ff3Gt Join by phone: 604-262-2433 Phone conference ID: 972 118 411# NOTES: NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COST ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO SAID NOTICE, ATTENDANCE AT THE VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY EVENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION SUBSEQUENTLY REQUESTED. You must be registered with the System for Award Management (SAM) in order to receive a Government contract award. To register, go to www.sam.gov. For additional information visit the website for the Federal Service Desk (www.FSD.gov) which supports SAM or contact them at 866-606-8220 for assistance.

title: Q&A for Third Party Liability (TPL) Insurance for All Embassy Vehicles (OFV)
description: 1.Could you please confirm whether the semiannual insurance premiums are payable in advance upon policy issuance and acceptance, or after completion of each six-month coverage period? Answer: The Government will award this solicitation as an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract. In line with local government policy, the Government will pay the full third-party liability (TPL) insurance premium one year in advance. If the Government adds a vehicle during the year, it will issue a task order, and the TPL insurance for that vehicle will cover only the days left in the policy year. 2. Please clarify whether invoices may be submitted at the beginning of each coverage period and the expected payment timeline following invoice acceptance. Answer: Please refer to Answer 1 3. Share your sponsor Number/computer Number if Commercial Registration is not available. Answer: The Embassy will give the applicable government registration number to the successful offeror at award. Offerors do not need this number to submit a proposal. 4. Fleet Details in Excel Format: Kindly provide an Excel file containing the details of all vehicles to be insured, including the following information for each vehicle: Serial Number Chassis Number (VIN) Vehicle Make and Type Model Year Answer: All of the requested information can be found in the main solicitation, with the exception of the serial numbers. Please see the attached Excel spreadsheet. 5. May a U.S.- registered company serve as the prime contractor while a licensed Saudi insurance company provides the policies, claims management, and legal services? Answer: The policies must be issued by an insurer licensed to underwrite motor insurance in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, as Saudi law requires. A non-insurer prime contractor may offer policies issued by a licensed Saudi insurer under a subcontract or teaming arrangement. The proposal must identify the insurer and include its license and Commercial Registration (CR) number. The prime contractor remains fully responsible for performance. 6. Would our previous experience in the UAE managing insurance for a fleet of 55 rental vehicles, together with the experience of a licensed Saudi insurance partner, satisfy the solicitation's past performance requirements? Answer: The Government will evaluate past performance under Section 4 evaluation criteria. The Government may consider the relevant past performance of proposed subcontractors or teaming partners who will perform major parts of the work. Offerors should describe how relevant their past contracts are in scope, size, and complexity. The Government does not decide in advance whether specific experience is acceptable. 7. Does the USD 55,000 contract maximum include VAT and all premiums for the 221 vehicles? Answer: The contract maximum of USD 55,000 all premiums for the 221 vehicles over. The Embassy is exempt from VAT / the Embassy reclaims VAT through the host-government refund program; offerors should price exclusive of VAT and show it as a separate line item. 8. Does Exhibit 1 represent the complete available claims history? If not, can additional loss-run information be provided? Answer: Exhibit 1 � Please find below the complete three years profit and loss ratio. 9. May the licensed Saudi insurance partner perform all claims administration and legal representation obligations on behalf of the prime contractor? Answer: A licensed Saudi insurer or subcontractor may perform claims administration and legal representation. The prime contractor remains fully responsible for meeting all contract obligations. The proposal must identify the entity that will perform these services.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Preventive Maintenance Service for One (1) Oxford Nanoimaging ONI Nanoimager
description: Title Preventive Maintenance Service for One (1) Oxford Nanoimaging ONI Nanoimager Description of Requirement The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI), intends to award a contract to Oxford Nanoimaging Inc on a sole-source basis pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, for the acquisition of Annual Service Plan - Nanoimager, the Government intends to solicit and award a Purchase Order on a sole-source basis because the Government's minimum technical requirements will be satisfied by Oxford Nanoimaging Inc. Tumor cells, immune cells, and irradiated tissues release large quantities of biologically active nanoscale extracellular vesicles (EVs). The Translational Nanobiology Section within the Laboratory of Pathology (LP) at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Cancer Institute (NCI), Center for Cancer Research (CCR), is developing new ways to investigate these EVs as biological agents, biomarkers, and therapeutic targets. The section uses an Oxford Nanoimaging (ONI) Nanoimager super-resolution microscope to provide high quality singlemolecule resolution imaging for nanoparticle analysis as part of the section�s EV production and analysis pipeline. Preventive maintenance services are required to ensure its highest peak performance, as this instrument is being used for developing guidelines for best practices in this area of research, and ultimately for establishing a foundation for next-generation EV-based personalized cancer treatment and monitoring. This acquisition is to acquire preventive maintenance services for a super resolution microscope system, Oxford Nanoimaging (ONI) Nanoimager, at the Laboratory of Pathology. Oxford Nanoimaging Inc (ONI) is the original manufacturer and sole provider of authorized maintenance services for the ONI Nanoimager super-resolution microscope. Due to the sensitive nature of the superresolution microscope, it can only be repaired by qualified, OEM-trained technicians. This specialized training is only accessible to Oxford Nanoimaging technicians. Furthermore, only Oxford Nanoimaging can provide access to genuine, proprietary OEM spare parts which are required to maintain this superresolution microscope. The OEM does not license 3rd party technicians, and spare or replacement parts for this instrument can only be obtained from the original manufacturer. Thus, no other vendor has trained personnel to work with this complex system or access to any potential required parts that might need replacing over time. Lastly, the operating system and software of this super-resolution microscope are proprietary and can only be serviced by Oxford Nanoimaging. All updates and patches are solely available through the OEM This makes Oxford Nanoimaging the only known source for this requirement and the only provider that can meet the Government�s needs at this time. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required supplies and meet all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to davisroshonna@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00010 in the subject line of the response

title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

The QX700 E Droplet Digital PCR System delivers the power of absolute quantification for our labs � without the need for standard curves. With simple setup, intuitive analysis, and 7-color multiplexing, it makes digital PCR more accessible than ever. All-in-one, integrated instrument enabling walkaway operation. Intuitive software with a user-friendly interface for easy run setup and data analysis. Generates absolute quantification results with intuitive software. A compact system built for low throughput or ad hoc studies and shared research spaces. Supports from 16, 32, or up to 48 samples per run, ensuring flexibility for low-throughput laboratories. description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) has a requirement for the demolition, removal, and replacement of existing Corian wall and floor systems in seasonal campground washrooms at Whistlers Campground, Jasper National Park To assist with bonding and insurance requirements, this project is estimated at a value between $500,001 > $1,000,000, Taxes extra. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI03 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor shall perform and complete the Work no later than March 26, 2027. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATION TESTING (EQT)
description: N00164-27-S-NC12 - REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/SOURCES SOUGHT � ENVIRONMENTAL QUALIFICATION TESTING (EQT) - PSC H270 - NAICS 541380 Issue Date: 29 OCT 2026 - Closing Date: 18 NOV 2026 - 11:00 AM EST REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) - The Government is issuing this RFI/sources sought announcement as part of market research for usage of Environmental Qualification Testing (EQT). The objective is to engage a qualified testing contractor to perform environmental qualification testing (EQT) to verify that this updated enclosure assembly and workstation mount meets all naval shipboard survival and operational requirements. The Statement of Work (SOW) defines the requirements for environmental and electromagnetic compatibility testing of the Combined All-Domain Command and Control System Afloat (CAC2S Afloat) Data Processing Assembly and Workstation Mount. See attached SOW to review the technical requirements provided as Attachment 1 to this document. Vendors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) and registered in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive access to the SOW. Information about the JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. In accordance with Department of Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS) Procedures, Guidance, and Information (PGI) 206.302-1, the Government is accepting information from companies potentially capable of meeting the requirements as described above. Companies with the capabilities and facilities to provide this testing that meets the Government�s requirements and certification requirements may respond. Responses shall address requirements as discussed within the SOW. All interested parties may submit company and product literature, a white paper no longer than 5 pages, and/or other pertinent information, such as a description with performance parameters and a statement of current availability, summary of prior testing, test reports, a budgetary estimate, and an explanation as to why the Government should not procure this effort on a sole source basis as stated above given the requirements set forth. Responses to the Market Survey shall include the following: Submitter�s Name Street Address, City, State, Zip Code Business Size Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone Announcement Number: N00164-27-S-NC12 Please include the purpose/explanation of the response to the Market Survey, i.e. to better understand the Government requirements; to potentially become a viable source for future requirements; to take exception to the anticipated sole source as your company currently meets all of the Government requirements. The Government may contact RFI respondents to get clarification on the information submitted. Submissions may be sent by any government or non- governmental entity including commercial firms, non-profit organizations, and institutions of higher education with degree-granting programs in science and/or engineering (universities), or by consortia comprising such concerns. Responses from Small and Small Disadvantaged Business firms are highly encouraged. Firms responding should indicate if they are a small business, a socially and economically disadvantaged business, 8(a) firms, historically black colleges or universities, and minority institutions. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government's System for Award Management (SAM) and in the Joint Certification Program (JCP) in order to receive the attachments. Offerors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.sam.gov. Information about on JCP is located at https://www.public.dacs.dla.mil/. At the current time, NO FUNDING IS AVAILABLE for contractual efforts. This RFI/sources sought does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The US Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Market Survey information may be submitted to the Point of Contact (POC) any time prior to the expiration of this announcement. The POC for this effort is Ms. Morgan Helton, morgan.m.helton.civ@us.navy.mil Responses to this RFI/sources sought may be emailed to the POC above. If any part of the submittal is classified, please contact the POC for appropriate submission information. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosures to non-government personnel and entities.

title: Groundwater Monitoring in Wabasha County, MN
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District is seeking a contractor to perform groundwater monitoring services in support of the Grand Encampment Dredge Material Placement Site Unload project along the Zumbro River near Kellogg, MN in Wabasha County. This solicitation is 100% set-aside for small business under NAICS 541380 with a size standard of $19 million. The contractor will collect water samples from three monitoring wells and up to four government-selected residential wells before, during and after the active unloading of the site in Spring 2027. During the active unload phase samples will also be collected from the river upstream of the site and from standing water within the active dredged-material placement/infiltration pit. Water samples will be analyzed by an environmental analytical testing laboratory accredited under the Minnesota Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (MNELAP) for all specified methods and parameters. Pre-Placement (Phase 1) samples will be collected and tested approximately 90, 60 and 30 days prior to the start of the active hydraulic transfer of stockpiled dredge materials to the upland placement site. Samples will be collected and tested during Active Placement (Phase 2) approximately 3, 17, and 31 days after the transfer begins, with options for additional sample collection and testing at approximately 45, 59 and 73 days after start of transfer. Post-Placement (Phase 3) samples will be collected and tested approximately 30, 60 and 90 days after the completion of the materials transfer. The contractor will prepare a final sampling and analysis report, submitted within 50 days of testing completion. All questions should be submitted in writing via the PIEE module Q and A section. Offers should be submitted via the PIEE Module. Click the first link in the Attachments/Links section.

title: 6515--Reprocessed Non-Critical Single Use Devices
description: THIS IS A COMBINED SYNOPSIS AND SOLICITATION NOTICE OF TIERED EVALUATIONS: This procurement action for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical/Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) Supplies Program and is set-aside based on an order of priority as established in 38 U.S.C. 8127. TIERED EVALUATIONS INCLUDING LARGE BUSINESS CONCERNS: This solicitation is being issued as a tiered evaluation with the following tiers: (1) SDVOSB concerns, (2) VOSB concerns, (3) small business concerns with HUBZone small business concerns and 8(a) participants having priority; and (4) large business concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is publishing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) on or about October 30, 2026, for the acquisition of consumable commodities in support of the Medical/Surgical Prime Vendor (MSPV) Program catalogue. The MSPV Program is a partnering effort between Veterans Healthcare Administration (VHA) and the VA Office of Acquisition, Logistics & Construction (OALC) to deliver a national strategic sourcing solution that combines a formulary approach with electronic cataloging and ordering of a wide range of medical and surgical supplies for the Veterans Administration Medical Centers (VAMC) and related facilities. The establishment of Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) is in direct support of this initiative and is a key element in the success of the MSPV Program, as the BPAs will provide the mechanism that will supply the types of supplies for distribution to all VHA facilities located in the United States (U.S.) and all U.S. Territories. In order to support the MSPV Program, the VA will establish BPAs for medical/surgical supplies through Open Market BPAs under FAR Part 12. This solicitation is structured as a tiered evaluation to maximize Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business and Veteran-Owned Small Business (SD/VOSB) participation. Quotations will be evaluated based on technical criteria and price. VHA clinicians will participate in evaluating all supplier quotations and awards will be made using comparative analysis. In order for an authorized distributor/supplier to participate in the MSPV Program, the authorized distributor/supplier and the Prime Vendor shall establish a Commercial Agreement within 60 days of award. The Commercial Agreement will govern the terms and conditions of the authorized distributor/supplier relationship and will not contradict the underlying terms and conditions established by this BPA or the underlying MSPV Contract. See Statement of Work for further details. The MSPV Program recognizes that various NAICS codes may/can be used for this procurement. The standard/typical NAICS code for surgical/medical supplies manufacturing (not including medical instruments or equipment) is 339113. Any future amendments and other miscellaneous documents will be available electronically for download at the following URL: http://www.sam.gov. No paper copies of the presolicitation/solicitation will be available, and no telephone requests for paper copies of the presolicitation/solicitation will be accepted. Interested Quoters are advised to continuously check the URL for any changes to this solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a quote that, if timely received NLT the due date and time for quote submission, will be given full consideration. MSPV is seeking quotes from authorized sources (including manufacturers) for each of the items on the quote sheet. The quote sheet for submission is found as Attachment A - Quote Sheet_36C24E27Q0005_Reprocessed SUDs_V1 and is the only acceptable quote sheet for submission. NOTE: All items are original equipment manufacturer products, and only the items listed can be quoted. MSPV is NOT seeking like or substitute items. Quotes for items not listed by OEM number on the quote sheet will not be accepted. If an item has been discontinued and a direct replacement is available, please provide that information to the Contracting Officer listed below. Be advised, the Government is not seeking substitute, equivalent, or like items at this time. Only direct replacements for discontinued items will be considered for this solicitation. If an item found within this solicitation classifies as a prosthetic item or is on another national-level VA contract vehicle please advise the Contracting Officer listed below. Any further questions may be directed to the Contracting Officer listed below. All questions and communications shall be in writing to the Contracting Officer at the email address listed below. Any revised/updated information received will be published as an amendment that revises/corrects the quote sheet. It is the burden of the quoter to continuously monitor this solicitation for any subsequent amendments. An Authorized Distributor Letter (ADL) from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) shall be included with all responses. The ADL from the OEM shall include each product(s) proposed authorizing the Quoter as a distributor for the proposed product(s). The letter must either state specific product(s) proposed or that the Quoter is an authorized distributor for all of OEM s products. title: Personal Radiation Detector (PRD)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) SUMMARY: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), Office of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) requires Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs). PRDs are pager-size devices worn by users for radiological and nuclear detection capability as well as personal protection. PRDs automatically monitor the environment and alert the user when radiation levels above the natural background are detected. PRDs also assist the user in localizing the source of detected radiation. The high sensitivity and rapid response time to the variations in the ambient radiation levels clearly distinguish PRDs from the family of electronic dosimeters which are mainly used for accurate dose and dose rate. GENERAL INFORMATION: This RFI is issued solely for information gathering purposes to identify offerors that can provide identify commercially available, gamma-detecting Personal Radiation Detectors (PRDs), including available wireless-communication and data-transmission capabilities in advance of an acquisition which will include testing of the most compliant candidate solutions. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), RFIs may be used when the Government wants to obtain price, delivery, other market information, and capabilities for planning purposes. Responses to these RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government for any purpose, nor does it restrict the Government to an ultimate acquisition approach. Respondents are solely responsible for all expenses associated with their RFI response. Respondents will not receive additional information in response to their submittal to the RFI and will not be notified of the resulting market research. Interested parties must submit sufficient documentation in accordance with the instructions in this RFI and current industry�s best practices and standards, demonstrating their ability/experience to meet or exceed the Government�s requirements listed in this notice. RFI RESPONSE SUBMITTAL INSTRUCTIONS: Interested contractors shall submit their RFI responses electronically to Isaac Chapple, Contracting Officer, at Isaac.Chapple@fema.dhs.gov no later than 12:00PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), (due 11/18/2026).

description: Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the Tactical Airlift Program Office (PMA-207), is conducting market research to identify responsible and qualified sources capable of furnishing PT6A-60A turboprop engines in either new production condition or overhauled condition meeting original equipment manufacturer (OEM) specifications and all applicable airworthiness, configuration-control, inspection, test, preservation, and technical-data requirements. The Government is seeking information from qualified vendors to include the OEM, OEM-authorized distributors, OEM-authorized maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) providers, and other responsible sources capable of supplying PT6A-60A engines for military aviation application. The Government seeks to identify potential business sources with the resources, capabilities, and experience necessary for the procurement of a PT6A-60A turboprop engine; and to obtain estimated procurement costs. Requested Industry Information: Interested sources are requested to submit a capabilities statement addressing the following: 1. Company Information Company name, address, CAGE code, UEI, and business-size status; Primary point of contact, telephone number, and email address; Identification of the respondent as OEM, authorized distributor, authorized MRO provider, or other source. 2. Technical Capability Demonstrated experience supplying new or overhauled PT6A-60A engines; Evidence of OEM authorization, distributorship, repair-station authorization, or other relevant qualification; Description of facilities, quality-management system, test-cell capability, and technical personnel; Description of the respondent�s configuration-control and parts-traceability processes; Ability to provide required engine records, airworthiness documentation, and certification documentation; Description of warranty terms and post-delivery technical support. 3.Schedule and Capacity Estimated lead time for new production engines; Estimated lead time for overhauled engines; Current and projected production/overhaul capacity; Identification of supply-chain risks, long-lead components, or other schedule constraints. 4. Commerciality and Pricing Information Whether the offered engine is customarily used by the general public or nongovernmental entities for purposes other than governmental purposes; Whether the item is sold competitively in substantial quantities in the commercial marketplace; Rough-order-of-magnitude pricing or commercial catalog/pricelist information, if available; Separate estimated pricing for new production and overhauled engines, if applicable; Recommended contract type, ordering approach, and warranty structure. 5. Small Business Participation Identification of any small-business teaming, subcontracting, distribution, overhaul, logistics, or sustainment capabilities relevant to this requirement; Recommendations for structuring a future acquisition to maximize competition and small-business participation, where practicable. Response Instructions: Responses should be submitted electronically in PDF format no later than 12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, to: Katelyn Campbell katelyn.e.campbell4.civ@us.navy.mil The email subject line shall read: "Sources Sought Response � PT6A-60A Turboprop Engine � [Company Name]" Respondents should clearly identify any proprietary information. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: https://www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the LPOE in Coburn Gore, ME must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 12:00 PM Eastern Time on 18 November 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. At minimum, the scope of services for this commission will require collaboration with the lead designer selected for the land port of entry project; travel to the project site; development and presentation of preliminary and final concepts; fabrication of the artwork; participation in meetings and conservation reviews as necessary; delivery and installation of the artwork; professional documentation of, and detailed maintenance planning for the artwork at the project site. For informational purposes: Artists selected for the contract award must be Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time of award. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 13934, agencies should prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded. Inquiries concerning the project should be directed to the following email address: Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov and reference the synopsis number in the subject line. No questions will be answered after 07 October 2026 12:00pm EST.

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4016 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the End of the World G-Z Long-Term IRSC (EOTW G-Z LTIRSC). The End of the World Project area is approximately 50,000 acres on the Salmon River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forest. The End of the World EIS authorizes commercial treatment on over 17,000 acres primarily through intermediate harvest. The purpose of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to thin overstocked stands to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfire as well as improve stand health. The EOTW Project is within the Wildland Urban Interface and has numerous private inholdings with seasonal and permanent residents. This contracting tool will increase the pace and scale of active management beyond the current capacity of staffing levels. A secondary objective of the EOTW G-Z LTIRSC is to provide a steady, dependable supply of timber and forest products to local facilities. This project aligns with Secretarial Memo 1078-006 and the Implementation of Secretarial Memo 1078-006 dated April 3, 2025 to utilize long term stewardship contracts for active management. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is an unrestricted requirement. All responsible sources may submit a proposal and offer which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

title: NGA HRM-II RFP
description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. title: Automated Ultrasound-Based, Super Intelligence (SI)-Enabled Fracture Detection
description: The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) for planning purposes. BARDA will not award any contracts under this Notice, but rather seeks current and forecasted prices, inventories, capabilities, and other pertinent marketplace data. This Notice is issued by the Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) to identify innovative medical countermeasure technologies to enable rapid triage of musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures and soft tissue injuries of extremities. This request is for information only and is intended to assess the current state of commercially available technologies and technologies nearing commercial availability that support automated ultrasound-based fracture detection using technologies commonly known as Artificial Intelligence (AI). Consistent with Executive Order 14434, �Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence,� AI- technologies are now referred to as Super Intelligence (SI) throughout this notice, including in the title and should be referred the same in the response. The Center for Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA) intends to use responses to this Sources Sought Notice (SSN) to inform planning for the potential acquisition of ultrasound-based devices capable of capturing and displaying anatomical data. Potential acquisition and inventory approaches include device purchases or leases supported by vendor-managed inventory (VMI) arrangements. BARDA seeks information on technologies that could assist clinical care providers in visualizing or detecting musculoskeletal injuries, including fractures and soft tissue injuries, to support triage and initial treatment in emergency departments, urgent care centers, and field settings. These devices could also support continued evaluation and treatment in definitive orthopedic care settings, consistent with applicable regulatory authorizations and intended uses. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) leads Federal public health and medical preparedness and response efforts, including supporting the research, development, acquisition, and availability of medical countermeasures (MCMs). These efforts address the health consequences of chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats, pandemic influenza, and emerging infectious diseases, including threats arising from deliberate, accidental, or naturally occurring events. This SSN supports planning for medical capabilities that could strengthen the Nation�s preparedness for and response to emergencies involving traumatic injuries. The Project BioShield Act of 2004 (Pub. L. No. 108-276) established authorities for procuring qualifying security countermeasures for the Strategic National Stockpile (SNS). The Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act of 2006 (Pub. L. No. 109-417) further strengthened the Nation�s medical countermeasure development and preparedness framework. The National Health Security Strategy 2023�2026 provides additional strategic context for strengthening preparedness, response, and recovery capabilities. Consistent with these preparedness objectives, this Sources Sought Notice seeks information on potential approaches to improve the availability and accessibility of relevant medical devices across health care settings. Approaches of interest include purchase, lease, vendor-managed inventory (VMI), and arrangements that combine access to devices with maintenance and readiness support. Information received will inform acquisition planning and assessment of these approaches, subject to applicable statutory authorities, acquisition requirements, and availability of funds. These documents represent the foundation for addressing the Nation�s CBRN MCM needs. Amongst the foundational documents referenced above, musculoskeletal injuries such as fractures resulting from nuclear blast explosions and structural collapse, as well as and other mass casualty events present significant challenges in both field and clinical settings which require prompt diagnosis for adjudication and triage of patients. Current standards of care rely heavily on radiography and CT imaging, which are often unavailable, delayed, or resource-constrained in austere environments, disaster response settings, or during patient surge conditions. Delayed or missed fracture diagnosis can worsen patient outcomes and burden downstream care. BARDA is seeking solutions that enhance the speed, accuracy, and accessibility of fracture detection at the point of injury and point of care, without dependence on traditional imaging infrastructure. CAPABILITY STATEMENT/INFORMATION SOUGHT This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) seeks information from small business (SB) and other than small business (OTSB) concerns regarding their qualifications, experience, and capabilities to develop, manufacture, and deploy standalone, point-of-care, super intelligence (SI)-enabled ultrasound devices for fracture detection. Respondents shall provide only the information, data, and materials necessary to demonstrate their capabilities relevant to this notice. Responses shall include separate Technical Representation and Business Representation sections, as detailed below. Each section shall not exceed 10 single-sided pages, including all attachments, r�sum�s, charts, and other supporting materials, and shall use 12-point Times New Roman font. Pages exceeding the limit for either section will not be reviewed. Respondents shall identify their business size status as either small business or other than small business under the NAICS code and corresponding size standard identified in this notice. Technical Representations Respondents shall provide the technical information requested by ASPR/BARDA in separately numbered sections, in the order listed below. As part of its market research, 181 MSG/MSC is issuing this Sources Sought to determine if there exist an adequate number of qualified interested contractors capable of providing the requirement. The Government may use the responses to this Sources Sought for information and planning purposes. The 181st IW has two fiber lines running through a manhole that need to be spliced to restore connectivity to one of our buildings. Due to the existing conditions, the contractor would need to have personnel who are qualified and equipped to enter the manhole/confined space, access the existing fiber, pull or work with the available slack, and complete the required fiber splicing and testing. The Defense Health Agency, Science and Technology Portfolio Management Division (STPMD) will co-sponsor a Forum on Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) hosted by the National Academy of Science, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM). The forum will provide STPMD on ongoing mechanism and neutral setting in which the full spectrum of Government stakeholders and public and private sector Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) to explore opportunities for collective action directed towards advancement in TBI care and research. The requirement contains a base year plus 4 option years. The NASEM will convene the Forum on TBI two (2) to three (3) times per year to provide and ongoing mechanism and neutral setting in which the full spectrum of Government stakeholders and public and private sector SMEs will share information and explore opportunities for collective action addressing contemporary topics in TBI and research. Forum members will address short- and long-term strategic planning for advancing TBI care and research spanning the full TBI continuum from prevention through acute care and rehabilitation. NASEM has established these forums as part of contract W81XWH22C0033. DHA is planning to participate as a key stakeholder. STPMD requires access to these Forums along with other military services and federal agencies. Any firm that believes it can provide the stated capability as outlined above are invited to submit a written notification to the Contracting Office NLT 2PM ET on 18 November 2026. Supporting evidence must be furnished in sufficient detail to demonstrate the firm�s ability to provide the stated capability. Information shall be sent electronically (via e-mail only) to Rich Trunnell, Contract Specialist, at richard.k.trunnell.civ@health.mil. No telephone requests will be accepted. Responses received will be evaluated; however; a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, DHACA will proceed with the sole sources contract.
