title: Idaho Panhandle National Forest UTV and Track Set Purchase- Amendment
description: Solicitation 1240BD27Q0006 is hereby amended via Amendment 0001 to clarify domestic sourcing requirements and extend the closing date. The purpose of this amendment is to provide critical clarifications regarding the Buy American Act (BAA) requirements for CLIN 0002 (All-Season Track Set) and to formally extend the response deadline. Key Changes and Clarifications: Domestic Origin Requirement (BAA): Both the Utility Task Vehicle (CLIN 0001) and the Track Set (CLIN 0002) must qualify as domestic end products manufactured in the United States. Brand Name / Visual Reference Clarification: Any references or images featuring foreign-manufactured brands (such as Camso) in the original solicitation were for illustrative performance benchmarking purposes only. Proposing foreign-manufactured track systems does not comply with federal sourcing restrictions. Offerors must propose an American-made equivalent. Closing Date Extension: Original Closing Date: October 28, 2026, at 11:00 AM PDT Revised Closing Date: November 18, 2026, at 11:00 AM PST Instructions to Offerors: Active offerors who previously submitted proposals are permitted to submit revised packages substituting non-compliant components with domestic equivalents. Revised offers must explicitly specify the manufacturer name and manufacturing facility location for both items. A signed copy of the SF-30 (Amendment 0001) must be included as Page 1 of the revised quotation package. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. Please review the attached SF-30 document for full details. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The U.S. Forest Service (USFS), Idaho Panhandle National Forests, has a requirement for the procurement and delivery of one (1) Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) and one (1) compatible all-season track kit. The equipment will be utilized by the Fire/Fuels program for wildland fire suppression and prescribed fire operations over severe, uneven terrain. All equipment must be delivered new, fully assembled, fluids serviced, and in a 100% turnkey state ready for immediate field deployment upon arrival. Note: The UTV does not have to arrive with the track set physically installed on the vehicle. However, the vehicle must be fully prepped and the track kit must arrive brand new, complete, and ready to be installed by a certified dealer To be considered responsive, contractors must submit combined pricing for both line items below: CLIN 0001: Utility Task Vehicle (UTV) Quantity: 1 EA Delivery Location: IDAHO PANHANDLE NATIONAL FORESTS SUPERVISORS OFFICE 3232 WEST NURSERY ROAD COEUR D'ALENE ID 83815 CLIN 0002: All-Season Track Kit Quantity: 1 EA Specifications: Must be 100% factory-compatible, field-interchangeable, and align directly with the vehicle awarded under CLIN 0001. Salient Characteristics (Minimum Technical Specifications) Proposed vehicles must meet or exceed the following design limits and features: Engine & Cooling: 4-stroke, liquid-cooled engine. Cylinder Displacement: Min: 998 cc | Max: 1500 cc. Horsepower: Min: 80 hp | Max: 150 hp. Dimensions: Length (120�138 in), Width (63�66 in), Height (76�82 in). Ground Clearance: Min: 13 in | Max: 20 in. Capacities: Person Capacity (2�3), Payload (1000�1700 lbs), Box Capacity (1000�1500 lbs), Towing Capacity (2500�3500 lbs). Tires: 8 to 10 ply; Size Min: 27 x 9 x 14 | Max: 30 x 11 x 15. Included Accessories/Features: Enclosed cab with full doors, hard top roof, glass full tip-out windshield with wipers, sliding window rear panel, heater/defroster, protection headache rack, front/rear a-arm protectors, skid plate, front/rear bumpers, fender flares, rock sliders, chainsaw mount, LED light bar, rearview mirror, and a >4,500 lb winch. Track Specs: Rubber tracks with a steel frame designed for all-season flotation/traction. Minimum 2-year warranty on tracks; minimum 1-year warranty on the UTV. Origin: Must be manufactured in the U.S. Delivery & Shipping Terms Delivery Timeline: All items must be physically delivered within 90 calendar days from the formal date of award. Shipping: FOB Destination. Pricing must be fully inclusive of all freight, handling, and delivery charges. The contractor is responsible for offloading equipment at the specified facility. No loading dock or equipment available to unload. UTV does not have to arrive with tracks installed but kit must be ready to be installed by a certified Evaluation and Basis for Award The Government will conduct a Side-by-Side Comparative Evaluation of quotes in accordance with simplified commercial procedures (FAR 12.201-1 and 12.205(c)(2)). Formal scoring matrices will not be used. A single Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract will be awarded based on the following factors: Technical Capability & Salient Characteristics: Degree to which the solution meets or exceeds design limits and accessory bundles. Delivery Timeline: Preference/favorable evaluation may be given to shorter delivery timelines than the mandatory 90 days. Price: Evaluated to ensure fairness and reasonableness. Submission Requirements Interested vendors must have an Active Registration in SAM (https://sam.gov) at the time of quote submission. Omitting a Unique Entity ID (UEI) will exclude the quotation package from consideration. Quotation packages must be organized in the following order and submitted via email to mindy.hickman@usda.gov: Failure to provide these documents will result in your offer being exluded from concideration. Spec sheets must be provided to complete an evaluation. SF-1449: Completed and signed (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c; including telephone, email, and SAM UEI in Block 17a). SF-30 Amendments: Acknowledged and signed (if any are posted by the CO). Schedule of Items: Completed pricing for CLIN 0001 and CLIN 0002. Technical Documentation: Drawings, spec sheets, or product brochures verifying compliance with salient characteristics. Closing Date for Receipt of Quotes: On or before 28 October 2026 no later than 11:00 AM PDT.

The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. description: The Defense Logistics Agency, Troop Support, Philadelphia, PA Medical Directorate intends to award a Firm Fixed Price, Sole Source contract under the authority of FAR 12.102(a) to Carahsoft Technology Corp, on behalf of Nuance, address 11493 Sunset Hills Road, Reston, VA 20190, for the procurement of the following brand name post warranty maintenance, updates, and software licensing Product: PowerScribe 360 post warranty maintenance, software licenses This award for brand name software licenses and post warranty maintenance will be placed on a sole source basis with Carahsoft, on behalf of Nuance, as the following circumstance in FAR 12.102(a) applies: only one source is available to provide the services required at the level of quality required because the services are unique or highly specialized. title: FLEXIBLE RUBBER PIPE COUPLINGS
description: Solicitation Modification 002: This amendment establishes the pre-award ship-check and field measurement requirements, clarifies the award consideration during technical evaluation, and the missing additional FAR clauses and provisions. 1. Pre-Award Ship Check and Field Measurements The Government does not possess reliable existing measurements; therefore, the performance requirement remains valid. Accordingly, offerors shall complete a ship check and conduct the necessary field measurements specified in the SOW, no later than November 16th, 2026, prior to the solicitation closing date of November 18th, 2026. This includes visually inspecting each of the twenty-four (24) target locations, verifying face-to-face dimensions, flange drilling patterns, allowable lateral/axial movement, adjacent clearances, and piping alignment necessary for off-site fabrication. Due to operational commitments and cutter availability, post-award access for obtaining measurements will not be feasible. Offerors are responsible for coordinating and completing any necessary ship check and field measurements before the established deadline to ensure their proposals are accurate and technically compliant. Requiring completion during the established availability window mitigates fabrication inaccuracies, improper fitting, schedule delays, and performance risk associated with the required delivery date of April 12, 2027. 2. Technical Evaluation and Award Eligibility Completion of the pre-award ship check and field measurements is a mandatory technical acceptability requirement. Offerors shall provide documentation of the completed site visit a technical approach, and technical capability demonstrating that their proposed offer is based on verified measurements meeting the SOW requirements. As previously stated, Firm Fixed Price Proposals shall be detailed and include information from the SOW demonstrating an understanding of all the requirements in the SOW. Proposals that fail to demonstrate compliance with this requirement by the established deadline will be determined technically unacceptable and ineligible for award, regardless of price. 3. Required Delivery Date The RDD remains on or before April 12, 2027. Offerors shall demonstrate their ability to fabricate and deliver the required components within the timeframe based on the verified ship-check measurements and anticipatory delivery date. 4. Additional FAR clauses and provisions. The original solicitation mentioned additional FAR clauses and provisions that was identified as missing. These have been included in an attachment as previously stated. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. The solicitation closing date and time of 18 November 2026 at 3:00 P.M. Eastern Standard Time remain unchanged. It is the responsibility of interested vendors to monitor the solicitation for any amendments, modifications, or other changes. End of Modification 002. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Solicitation Modification 001: This solicitation amendment is to address the Statement of Work file attachment. Multiple interested vendors reported not being able to review the SOW word doc file format. The SOW attachment has been uploaded under PDF file format. All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. The solicitation closing date and time of 18 November 2026 at 3:00 P.M. Eastern Standard Time remain unchanged. title: Request for Information for U-2 Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System -2
description: Amendment 1- Response due date was updated to Nov 18, 2026 03:00 pm EST. The RFI attachment has been updated. The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the repair data, expertise, capabilities, manufacturing, engineering, software development, maintenance and experience to meet qualification requirements to repair and sustain the Advanced Synthetic Aperture Radar System (ASARS)-2 components and ground support equipment. The level of security clearance and amount of overseas continental United States participation in this requirement has not been determined. The Government does not own or have access to the data for the ASARS-2 sensor. The Government has determined that this system is a noncommercial item. The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the ASARS-2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval to The Air Force requires long-term support and sustainment of the ASARS-2, which provides near-real-time high-resolution, long-range imagery from ground returns during day or night, in all weather conditions. Air Combat Command A5 requirements provide for an over-arching sustainment program for the U-2. The Contract Logistics Support (CLS) includes engineering support, the repair of spare assets, resolution of system failures and issues to ensure availability, reliability, and maintainability of the fielded equipment and software. This effort requires cybersecurity support and sustainment in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 503, and the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) process, Cybersecurity Impact Evaluation Recommendation (CIER) for all changes and modifications of this effort to incorporate in the U-2S Approval toOperate (ATO) package, Cybersecurity Authorization Package (CAP), Risk Management Framework (RMF), Interim Authority to Test (IATT), Interim Authority to Connect (ATC), and/or separate ATO, as applicable and requested by the Government. This effort also requires Depot Maintenance Support Teams (DMST) to support the following sustainment activities: mission software updates; Diminishing Manufacturing Sources (DMS) engineering; engineering change proposals; configuration management (hardware and software); integration with ASARS-related systems on the U-2 platform; data management; technical data (such as technical manuals and reports) development and maintenance; in-plant Specialized Repair Activity and sparing; technical and engineering actions for calibrating ASARS-2; resolving system failures/issues in a timely manner; and planning/preparation/implementation of system sustainment improvements.

title: Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YON-325
description: The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) is conducting market research to determine industry capability and interest in performing the maintenance, repair, and preservation of YON-325. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. The Government is seeking responses from sources that can perform the following work. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. YON-325 � Length: 199 FT � Width: 54 FT � Height: 15 FT � Age: 21 YRS � Hull Type: Steel � Draft: 3 FT � Full Displacement: 2,848 L Tons � Light Load: 706 L Tons Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel from Manchester Fuel Depot to the Contractor�s facility. Dock, wash, and clean exterior surfaces of the vessel upon docking. Replace zinc anodes on hull / Skegs. Accomplish preservation to Underwater Hull, Freeboard, Main deck, Deck house, Cargo piping and all deck fittings. Clean non-skid located Main deck, Deck house top and Cargo deck. Remove, clean and install Rubber fenders. Modify existing Piping eliminate Aft Flow Meter and insert spool. Accomplish Ultrasonic test measurement and visual inspection of the hull, Main deck, Cargo deck and Deck house top. Open, Clean, Pump and maintain clean and dry each tank/void. Inspect tanks/voids for defects Refresh Exhaust Muffler for Yanmar and Main Engine. Replace Solar Panels. Remove Antenna Support Modification. Replace Fuel Oil Tank Piping. Replace and Calibrate Cargo Tank Level Indicator�s (TLI�s). Perform Preliminary Air test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish a final closure inspection of each tank/void upon completion of all work installing new gaskets and fasteners. Perform Final Air Test of Tanks/voids/Steel Fendering and Skegs. Accomplish repair, replace gaskets, and adjust watertight hatches and doors. Accomplish Cargo Pump Diesel and Diesel generator maintenance and repair. Undock the vessel. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. Calibration of TLI�s, shall be conducted at Manchester Fuel Depot (MFD) in Manchester, WA. YON-325 Prime Period of Performance: Estimated August 2027 through November 2027 What/Where to Submit: Interested companies should submit, on company letterhead, a notice of interest including the name, telephone number, mailing address, and e-mail address of one point of contact. Please hand or digitally sign your letter of interest and e-mail it to the Government contacts listed below, with "Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YON-325 Sources Sought Response" in the subject field. The notice of interest should include a brief description of your company and its capabilities as they relate to the requirements set forth in the description shown above, and answers to the following specific questions. Please limit your response to no more than 5 pages. 1. Is your company a small or large business as defined by the Small Business Administration (SBA) under NAICS code 336611 (a small business must have 1,300 or less employees)? 2. Does your company have a satisfactory performance record for the type of work required? Please provide examples of relevant and recent (within three years) past performance. 3. Does your company have the necessary organization, experience, accounting and operational controls, and technical skills, or the ability to obtain them (including, as appropriate, such elements as production control procedures, property control systems, quality assurance measures, and safety programs applicable to materials to be produced or services to be performed by the prospective contractor and subcontractors)? 4. Given the work described in this announcement, does your company plan to submit a quotation in response to the anticipated solicitation for the Maintenance, Repair, and Preservation of YON-325 package? 5. Does your company have a current Agreement for Boat Repair (ABR) or Master Ship Repair Agreement (MSRA)? When to Submit: Responses are requested no later than 12:00PM PT, on 18 November 2026. Notice Regarding Sources Sought: This sources sought is issued solely for information and planning purposes - it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ) or a promise to issue an RFQ in the future. This sources sought does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Navy is not seeking quotations at this time, nor accepting unsolicited quotations. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this source sought; all costs associated with responding to this source sought will be solely at the interested party's expense. Not responding to this sources sought does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM website (sam.gov). It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Information provided shall be treated as Business Sensitive or Confidential to the responder, exempt from public release under the Freedom of Information Act. PSNS&IMF may request further information regarding the capabilities of respondents to meet the requirements set forth in the announcement. Information provided in response to this sources sought announcement will not be considered an offer by the responding contractor and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

title: Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - New Jersey, on behalf of the office of the Project Manager, Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs) in support of the M777A2 155mm Howitzer. The PFM Assembly consists of three assemblies: (1) Body Assembly, (2) Tray Assembly, and (3) Magazine Assembly, and each assembly consists of several sub-assemblies. In addition to the PFM Assembly, the Dog Coupler Assembly (legacy), Reinforced Dog Coupler Assembly, Magazine Primer Stop, Injector Arm Assembly, Firing Pin, Cross Pin, and Inert Primers are considered down parts to the overarching PFM assemblies.Specifications: The contractor shall manufacture, test, and deliver Primer Feed Mechanism (PFM) assemblies and associated components for the M777A2 Lightweight 155mm Howitzer to support U.S. or Foreign Military Sales customers. Specific detailed packaging instructions will be included on the delivery order on a case-by-case basis.Planned Acquisition: The Government intends to award a single, five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) delivery orders with five one-year Ordering Periods (OPs) from Fiscal Year (FY) 27-32. The production contract award will be based upon Full and Open Competition as a 100% Small Business Set Aside, in accordance with FAR 19.5.The following Ordering Periods are anticipated:OP 1: 12 months from date of awardOP 2: 12 months from the end of OP 1OP 3: 12 months from the end of OP 2OP 4: 12 months from the end of OP 3OP 5: 12 months from the end of OP 4. **This is a notice that Solicitation W15QKN-26-R-A044 is being placed on hold until further notice. The Government will provide notice when the solicitation is active again. For administrative purposes, the closing date is extended to November 18, 2026, to prevent system closure. Proposal submission is not required until further notice.**

To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210). One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective vendors navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), NCAGE, and PIEE registration. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. description: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to remove and replace ten (10) existing inpatient restroom Patient Care Units (PCUs) with VA-approved fixed-type toilet, sink, cabinet, and countertop assemblies. Work includes demolition of existing units, reuse of existing plumbing connections, wall repair and painting, installation of new PCUs, and installation of new privacy curtain tracks and curtains. All work shall be performed in an occupied healthcare environment while minimizing disruptions to facility operations and maintaining access to adjacent spaces. The required period of performance is 180 calendar days from Notice to Proceed.

title: INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT (LIMA, PERU): DAY 2 � CONSTRUCTION
description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) � LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 2 � CONSTRUCTION Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - Construction Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV9 NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Associated Sources Sought: W51DQV27S1CQ0 Event Date: Wednesday, December 2, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210) This announcement specifically covers Day 2 (Construction). Separate announcements address Day 1 (A/E Services) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the planned Design-Build construction requirements for the shoreside modernization at Callao, brief prospective prime contractors and subcontractors on USACE contracting and technical standards, explain federal registration procedures, and conduct one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: Construction: A comprehensive briefing on project scope, facility packages, technical specifications, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance requirements. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective Prime Contractors to present capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition team. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective contractors navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and NCAGE. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. Logistics & Schedule Date: December 2, 2026 Hours: 08:30 � 4:00 PM AT/Local Lima Time Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja Av. San Luis S/N� Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event. Event Details & Specific Sessions Session 1: Construction Seminar & Project Scope Briefing USACE project and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering: Detailed project background and site layout for the Callao Naval Base. Design-Build technical parameters, civil and structural works, industrial warehousing, and specialized mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP) systems. Acquisition milestones, contract structure, evaluation criteria, and Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements. Practical guidance on doing business with USACE and U.S. Federal Government contracting standards. Session 2: One-on-One Capability Briefings (Pre-Registration Required) Prospective Prime Contractors (including formal Joint Ventures and Prime Mentor-Prot�g� partnerships) may request a dedicated 15-minute private session with the USACE acquisition panel. Objective: Market research to assess industry interest, bonding capacity, construction methodologies, and regional execution capabilities. Eligibility: Strictly reserved for entities intending to submit a proposal as a Prime Contractor. Availability: Time slots are limited and will be confirmed on a strictly first-come, first-served basis upon receipt and validation of the RSVP form. Session 3: Federal Systems Registration Support Throughout the day, USACE specialists will host an individual support station to assist contractors with: Companies interested in receiving support should bring a computer. Navigating NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code applications. Obtaining a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and activating an account in SAM.gov. Project & Requirement Overview Project Description The contemplated acquisition will be executed as a complete Design-Build (D-B) contract. The scope of work encompasses: Post-award architectural and engineering final design. Geotechnical verification, bulk earthwork, site preparation, and foundation stabilization. Civil infrastructure, perimeter security, access roadways, and heavy-duty utility integration. Structural construction of industrial logistics, storage, and administrative facilities. Advanced mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), climate-control, fire suppression, and cold-chain systems. Complete Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E) packages. Statutory Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance coverage and host-nation environmental/building compliance. Summary of Facility Packages Building 110 Primary Function: Spare Parts Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Primary Function: Clothing & Gear Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Primary Function: Material Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Primary Function: Customs Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Primary Function: Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Primary Function: Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 Primary Function: DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Key Technical Considerations: Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Primary Function: Infrastructure & Integration Key Technical Considerations: Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. Streamlined RSVP & Venue Access Instructions Due to facility capacity constraints and military installation security protocols at Centro Naval, advance registration is mandatory. Attendance is limited to a maximum of three (3) representatives per company. description: US ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS (USACE) � LATIN AMERICA AND CARIBBEAN DISTRICT INDUSTRY DAY ANNOUNCEMENT: DAY 1 � ARCHITECTURE & ENGINEERING (A/E) SERVICES Requirement: Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization - AE Customer Agency: Peruvian Navy Notice ID: W51DQV27Z1CV8 NAICS Code: 541330 � Engineering Services Event Date: Wednesday, December 1, 2026 Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja, Lima, Peru RSVP Deadline: November 18, 2026, at 3:00 pm CT General Overview The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Caribbean District, is hosting an Industry Day event in Lima, Peru, to engage with industry partners regarding the upcoming acquisition of the Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project and NAMRU-S O&M Project. To provide focused engagement for distinct industry sectors, the event is structured over three specialized days: Day 1 (Tuesday, December 1, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Architecture & Engineering (A/E) Services (NAICS 541330) Day 2 (Wednesday, December 2, 2026): Callao Naval Base, Peru, Infrastructure Modernization Project - Construction (NAICS 236220) Day 3 (Thursday, December 3, 2026): U.S. Navy Medical Research Unit South (NAMRU-S) Lima and Iquitos, Peru - Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M) Services (NAICS 561210) This announcement specifically covers Day 1 (A/E Services). Separate announcements address Day 2 (Construction) and Day 3 Facilities Operation and Maintenance (O&M). Purpose of the Event The purpose is to present the planned Architectural and Engineering (A/E) requirements in support of shoreside and port facility modernization at Callao Naval Base, brief prospective prime design firms and specialized consultants on USACE engineering criteria and U.S. Federal contracting standards, provide walk-in technical guidance on federal vendor registrations, and conduct private one-on-one market research capability briefings. Summary of the Sessions The program includes three distinct sessions: A/E Design: A comprehensive briefing detailing project scope, facility design packages, site conditions, host-nation and DoD design standards, BIM requirements, procurement timelines, and USACE compliance guidelines. One-on-One Capability Briefings: Private, scheduled 15-minute briefings reserved for prospective A/E firms to present specialized technical and managerial capabilities directly to the USACE acquisition panel. Federal Systems Registration Support: Individual, walk-in technical assistance to help prospective firms navigate SAM.gov, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and NCAGE. Please note: This announcement is issued solely for market research and informational planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), an Invitation for Bids (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the U.S. Government. No contract award will result directly from this event. Logistics & Schedule Date: December 1, 2026 Hours: 08:30 � 4:00 PM CT/Local Lima Time Location: Centro Naval Sede San Borja Av. San Luis S/N� Cdra. 24, Urb. San Borja Sur, Lima, Peru Daily Schedule Note: A detailed schedule of presentations, networking intervals, and allocated session times is currently being finalized. The specific daily agenda will be published in a forthcoming update to this announcement prior to the event. Event Details & Specific Sessions Session 1: A/E Seminar & Design Scope Briefing USACE engineering, project management, and contracting representatives will deliver a detailed technical presentation covering: Master planning, site layout, and architectural vision for the Callao Naval Base modernization. Design criteria, geotechnical and seismic considerations, coastal environment durability standards, and Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC). Building Information Modeling (BIM), specialized mechanical/electrical/plumbing (MEP), fire protection, environmental permitting, and host-nation building codes. Overview of the federal A/E Brooks Act selection process (FAR Part 36.6), evaluation criteria, submission requirements (Standard Form 330), and milestone schedules. Session 2: One-on-One Capability Briefings (Pre-Registration Required) Prospective A/E firms (including formal Joint Ventures and Prime Mentor-Prot�g� partnerships) may request a dedicated 15-minute private session with the USACE technical and acquisition panel. Objective: Market research to assess industry interest, multi-disciplinary engineering depth, regional design experience, BIM/CADD capabilities, and past performance. Availability: Time slots are limited and will be confirmed on a strictly first-come, first-served basis upon receipt and validation of the RSVP form. Session 3: Federal Systems Registration Support Throughout the day, USACE specialists will host an individual support station to assist contractors with: Firms interested in receiving support should bring a computer Navigating NATO Commercial and Government Entity (NCAGE) code applications. Obtaining a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and activating an account in SAM.gov. Project & Requirement Overview Project Description The contemplated acquisition covers comprehensive multi-disciplinary Architecture and Engineering (A/E) services. The scope of work encompasses: Topographic, hydrographic, and geotechnical site investigations and soil stabilization analysis. Comprehensive seismic engineering compliant with Peruvian seismic zones and DoD structural criteria. Concept development, 35% preliminary design, 65% intermediate design, and final 100% ready-to-advertise design packages and technical specifications. Multi-discipline engineering including civil, structural, architectural, MEP, specialized fire suppression, industrial ventilation, cold-chain refrigeration, and telecommunications. Environmental assessments, stormwater management planning, and host-nation regulatory compliance support. Complete Furniture, Fixtures, & Equipment (FF&E) interior design packages. Development of construction cost estimates (MII format) and construction phasing schedules. Summary of Facility Packages: Building 110 Primary Function: Spare Parts Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Heavy-duty slab design, industrial racking integration, material handling flow, automated logistics staging. Building 115 Primary Function: Clothing & Gear Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: High-density pallet storage, humidity and climate control, inventory distribution bays. Building 112 Primary Function: Material Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Bulk staging, overhead crane/hoist accommodations, heavy equipment ingress/egress ramps. Building 113 Primary Function: Customs Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secure bonded holding areas, host-nation customs inspection layout, physical security infrastructure. Building 114 Primary Function: Petroleum, Oil, and Lubricants (POL) Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Secondary containment, explosion-proof electrical systems, specialized foam/water fire suppression, environmental drainage controls. Building 111 Primary Function: Medicine & Medical Supplies Warehouse Key Technical Considerations: Temperature/humidity-controlled storage (cold chain capability), pharmaceutical-grade clean finishings, backup power integration. Building 120 Primary Function: DIRNOTEMAT & Quality Control Building Key Technical Considerations: Administrative offices, testing and quality inspection laboratories, specialized testing benches, IT/telecom infrastructure. Site & Ancillary Works Primary Function: Infrastructure & Integration Key Technical Considerations: Site grading, structural fill, perimeter security, access roads, utility connections, complete FF&E packages, and host-nation compliant permitting. title: Tax Software and Support
description: The IRS has an ongoing requirement for commercial tax software products and associated services supporting the Federal Tax Compliance mission. The anticipated contract will provide software licenses, customization, software maintenance, integration, training, and user and technical support. The requirement includes, but is not limited to: Up to 130 Tax Analyzer licenses and annual renewals; Up to 150 Tax Planner licenses and annual renewals; Tax software user and technical support/help desk services; Maintenance of IRS-customized Issue Management System (IMS) Tax Engine Middleware; Support and maintenance of the Tax Engine Middleware Plug-In; Software customization and integration; Annual face-to-face training for up to 25 participants; Quarterly virtual training for licensed users; Software updates, upgrades, patches, and enhancements; Integration and testing support; and Associated program management, cybersecurity, documentation, and technical support services. Anticipated Period of Performance Base Period: December 18, 2026 - December 17, 2027 Option Period 1: December 18, 2027 - December 17, 2028 Option Period 2: December 18, 2028 - December 17, 2029 Option Period 3: December 18, 2029 - December 17, 2030 Option Period 4: December 18, 2030 - December 17, 2031 The government anticipates awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract utilizing a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection approach in accordance with FAR 15.101-1. Proposals will be evaluated based on the following factors, listed in descending order of importance: Technical Approach Licensing, Middleware Integration & Support Capability Past Performance Price The combined non-price factors are significantly more important than price. Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the government, considering price and non-price factors. The government intends to award without discussions; however, it reserves the right to conduct discussions if determined necessary by the Contracting Officer. Questions and Proposal Submission Questions Due: October 30, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. Proposals Due: November 18, 2026, at 4:00 PM Eastern Time. All questions and proposals shall be submitted electronically via email to both: louis.c.browniii@irs.gov tanya.r.burnett@irs.gov Offerors shall submit proposals in accordance with Section L, Instructions, Conditions, and Notices to Offerors, and Section M, Evaluation Factors for Award, of the attached solicitation. Interested offerors are encouraged to carefully review the solicitation and all accompanying attachments for complete technical requirements, proposal instructions, evaluation criteria, and applicable terms and conditions. Any amendments, clarifications, or updates to this solicitation will be posted on SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for updates and amendments throughout the solicitation period.

title: Austempered Ductile Iron (ADI) 5 Inch Projectile Bodies
description: The Naval Surface Warfare Center, Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), Contracts Department intends to issue a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract on a sole source basis to Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation. The NAICS is 332993. The Contractor shall develop and produce new Austempered Ductile Iron (ADI) 5 Inch Projectile Bodies compatible with the MK 45 Gun Weapon System. In accordance with 10 USC �4022, the Government will be awarding a follow-on FAR contract. The Naval Energetic Systems and Technologies (NEST) Request for Prototype Projects (RPP), under which this prototype OTA was awarded, included provisions for a follow-on production contract. The prototype OTA award for the ADI 5 Inch Projectile Bodies development and qualification was competitively awarded and the associated tasks mentioned above were delivered successfully and accepted by the Government as the basis for the prototype build. The participant in the OTA (Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation) successfully completed the prototype projects provided for in N001742390042. As such, the requirements of 10 USC �4022(f)(1) and DFARS 206.001-70 have been met and a follow-on contract for production can proceed without further competition. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR 15.201(e), THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE IN DETERMINING ITS ACQUISITION APPROACH. THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH. The documents below contain a description of the Cross Over Network requirements, technical data package, and a Contractor Capability Survey. The Survey allows Contractors to provide their company's capability. Attention Small Business Respondents who are interested in participation for this effort: 1. No set aside decision has been made; however, the USG will determine the final strategy after thorough analysis of the small business responses and other market research available, considering the demonstrated interest and capability. Please ensure that you provide a thorough response to each question. If you company does not currently possess the full capability required to fulfill the entire requirment, what teaming/partnership/joint venture/subctonracting arrangements do you have in place to fulfill the Government's needs? Provide evidence of this arrangement e.g. emails, letter, etcl. that demonstrate a united response to this Sources Sought is highly encouraged, but not required. The evidence should state the type of arrangement and the role each member will fulfill. If you are only interested in being a subcontractor to the future awardee, state the portion of the work your organization has capability of fulfilling. 2. Identify any areas of work that your organization believes should be broken out exclusively for Small Businesses. Both Large and Small Businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint Ventures or Teaming Arrangements are encouraged. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Brandon Jones, Contracting Officer, AFLCMC/ESGK-R (brandon.jones.96@us.af.mil) and Elizabeth Fuller (elizabeth.fuller.2@us.af.mil), Lead System Engineer, and Robert Cowden (robert.cowden.ctr@us.af.mil). title: Turf Application Services at Salisbury National Cemetery
description: GENERAL INFORMATION: Document Type: Combined Synopsis Solicitation Solicitation Number: 36C78627Q0021 Title: Turf Application Services at Salisbury National Cemetery Post Date: 10/26/2026 Original Response Date: 11/18/2026 at 4:00 pm EST Applicable NAICS: 561730 Landscaping Services PSC: S208 Housekeeping Landscaping/Groundskeeping Set Aside Type: Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Issuing Contracting Office: Department of Veterans Affairs National Cemetery Administration, Contract Services 18434 Joplin Road Triangle, VA 22172 Place of Performance: Salisbury (Annex) National Cemetery 501 Statesville Blvd Salisbury, NC 28144 Attachments: A Statement of work (pg 10) B - Price Schedule (pg 23) C SCA Wage Determination 2015-4423 Rev. 35 (pg 31) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with FAR Overhaul Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 36C78627Q0021 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for turf-care supplies and application services at Salisbury National Cemetery. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 with an effective date of 03/13/2026. NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRIAL CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE: The (NAICS) code for this procurement is 561730. The business size standard in millions of dollars is $9,500,000. PRICE SCHEDULE: See Attachment B. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: See Statement of Work at Attachment A. CONTRACT DATES: The period of performance will be a twelve-month base year and two (2) one-year options, if exercised, from date of award. DELIVERY/ACCEPTANCE LOCATION: Delivery and acceptance locations will be at the Place of Performance addresses listed on page 1 of this Combined Synopsis/Solicitation. CONTRACT TYPE: The U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs, National Cemetery Administration, anticipates the award of a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) contract for turf application services at Salisbury National Cemetery. This notice shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to ultimately award a contract, nor does it restrict the Government to a particular acquisition approach. This solicitation and the subsequent award is subject to the availability of funding. PRE-QUOTE SITE VISIT: Quoters are urged and expected to inspect all sites where services are to be performed and to satisfy themselves regarding all general and local conditions that may affect the cost of contract performance. In no event shall failure to inspect one or all sites constitute grounds for a claim after contract award. If you plan to conduct a site visit/inspection of the Salisbury National Cemetery, the following site visits have been scheduled: Salisbury (Annex) National Cemetery - Thursday, November 5, 2026 @ 10:00 a.m. EST. *No additional site-visits or individual tours will be scheduled. Interested prospective quoters should attend the scheduled site visit. Please meet Timothy Jones at the entrance of the cemetery. A RSVP is not required for the site visit. All questions resulting from the site visit should be sent to the Contracting Officer by following the instructions in the RFQ QUESTIONS section of this Combined Synopsis Solicitation. The Contracting Officer will then issue an amendment(s) answering all questions that were received on time (by the question due date). Potential Quoters are responsible for checking SAM.gov for issued Amendments to this Combined Synopsis Solicitation. INSTRUCTIONS TO QUOTERS: All prospective Quoters are required to have an active Federal Government contracts registration in System for Award Management (SAM) website when they submit a quote, and at time of award. If a Quoter does not have an active/current registration with SAM.gov prior to the solicitation close date, and at time of award, it will result in the company being considered non-responsive. Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) socio-economic category concerns MUST also have an active/current registration with SBA Small Business Search (https://search.certifications.sba.gov/) prior to the solicitation close date, and at time of award. Failure to comply will result in the Quoter being considered ineligible. RFQ QUESTIONS: All questions regarding this solicitation are to be submitted to the Contracting Officer, via email, no later than 4:00 pm EST, Monday, November 9, 2026. No questions will be accepted after this time. Questions pertaining to this announcement shall be sent by email to: sarah.poole1@va.gov. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted. Amendments will be issued to answer all questions that are submitted. RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR QUOTATION (RFQ): Quotes are due to the Contracting Officer no later than 4:00 pm EST on Wednesday, November 18, 2026. Email responses to sarah.poole1@va.gov and Antionette.Collins@va.gov. Responses to this announcement may result in a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) contract. The Government intends to make award without discussions. It is the responsibility of the Quoter to submit their best pricing at the time quotes are due. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary and the Government will not pay for information provided nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided for the Government. Quoters are responsible for obtaining any and all amendments or additional information concerning this announcement at SAM.gov. Failure to provide a signed amendment as part of the quotation submission will result in being considered non-responsive and therefore ineligible for award. QUOTATION FORMAT AND SUBMITTAL INFORMATION: Quotes must be submitted on company letterhead in Adobe pdf platforms and submitted by email to the individual listed in the Response to Request for Quotation (RFQ) section of this Combined Synopsis Solicitation. Quoters are hereby advised that any Quoter-imposed terms and conditions which deviate from the Government s terms and conditions, shall render the Quoter s quote non-responsive, and thus ineligible for award. All quotes shall be submitted in three (3) different documents for each volume listed below. Each title shall include the appropriate Volume. The Volumes are as follows: Volume A Administrative The Quoter shall include the following in Volume A: Legal Business/Company Name (as listed in SAM.gov) Business Mailing Address SAM Unique Entity ID (UEI) Point of Contact Telephone Number Email Address Signed and dated copy of each Amendment, if applicable. Failure to comply shall result in the Quoter being considered non-responsive and thus ineligible for award. Completed copy of the following clause is required to be submitted as part of the quote: (Failure to comply shall result in the Quoter being considered non-responsive). VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction (OCT 2026) (DEVIATION) *NOTE It is the responsibility of the Quoter to ensure the required entity-level representations and certifications are completed on SAM.gov, and that all other (procurement specific & by submission of the Offeror) required representations and certification provisions are submitted with their quotation. (Those listed above must be submitted with the quote, unless disclosure is not required.)
